title: Batch Generation Workflow Stepper
description: A step-through of the eight steps of the MicroSim generator skill's batch workflow that shows each step's command, input file, output file and lifecycle state, and explains why a script, the agent or a human checkpoint performs it. An optional Predict first mode asks the learner to predict the actor before revealing it.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Educational Technology
Instructional Design
AI-Assisted Content Generation
MicroSim Engineering

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
educational.topic: Batch generation workflow of the MicroSim generator skill
learningObjectives: The learner will explain what each step of the batch generation workflow does and why it is done by a script or by the agent.
prerequisites: Parts of a MicroSim folder (main.html, index.md, metadata.json, the .js file)

accessibility.screenReaderDescription: describe() summarizes the eight steps, the color key and the controls
accessibility.colorIndependent: Each step box also prints its actor as a word

controls.label: Reset
controls.action: Return to step 1 and clear predictions

controls.label: Predict first
controls.action: Hide each step's actor until the learner predicts it

controls.label: Script / Agent / Human
controls.action: Record a prediction for the selected step (Predict first mode only)

controls.label: Step box
controls.action: Select a step; hover shows its one-line purpose

variables: lifecycle state (specified, scaffolded, implemented, validated, deployed)
assumptions: Step names, commands and lifecycle states follow the batch route described in Chapter 5 and the generator skill's SKILL.md.
limitations: Commands are shown in shortened form without the --project-dir and --verbose options.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through worked example with optional predict-first prompts
keyQuestions: Why are six of the eight steps done by scripts?
What makes writing the JavaScript file the one step that needs the agent?
At which steps does the skill stop and hand a decision to a person?
commonMisconceptions: The AI agent does every step of the workflow.
The layout review is fully automatic and needs no human judgment.
Inserting iframes by itself makes a MicroSim deployed.
assessmentOpportunities: Predict first score across the eight steps
One-sentence explanation of why each step belongs to its actor
